Cloudflare IS present in front (cf-ray on every response, server:cloudflare) but the BLOCKING WAF firing the XSS rule is Wordfence — not Cloudflare managed rules. R1's wafProbeEvidence.wordfenceInBody:false is CONTRADICTED by the body content. R1 saw the 403+17925-byte signature but did not grep the body. The DB value (cloudflare-passive) has the same blind spot. Normal crawler traffic still 200 (Wordfence rule-selective on payload), so hasWaf can stay false operationally OR be set to true defensively, but wafType must reflect the actual blocker.

WC Store API DEFAULT behavior (no stock_status filter) EXCLUDES out-of-stock products. Verified live: GET /wp-json/wc/store/v1/products?include=263618,263616,263612 (3 known OOS ids) returns []; same request with stock_status=instock,outofstock returns all 3. worker.ts:452-457 sends params: { include: ids, per_page: CHUNK_SIZE } with NO stock_status param — therefore inherits Store API's default in-stock filter. Consequence: if a previously-in-stock product transitions OOS, store-api verify returns empty -> product wrongly flagged missing/deleted. JSON-LD per-product verify is robust to this: confirmed application/ld+json @type:Product with InStock/price markers on product pages. DB operator chose json-ld for this reason. R1's SKILL.md-default recommendation overlooks this site-specific stock-visibility behavior.

Live probes today: /wp-json/wc/store/v1/products?per_page=1 -> x-wp-total: 4493 (in-stock visible). /wp-json/wp/v2/product?per_page=1 -> x-wp-total: 11370 (all publish). /wp-json/wc/store/v1/products?per_page=1&stock_status=instock,outofstock,onbackorder -> x-wp-total: 11370 (matches admin). 4493 + 6877 (OOS) = 11370 -> sums verified. Both R1's 4493 and DB's 11411 are wrong in opposite directions: R1 picked the in-stock-only subset; DB has 41-item drift from 33-day-old recording. The TRUE total of published products is 11370. The IN-STOCK subset (matches what /shop/ HTML shows and what customers see) is 4493. Recommend keeping productCountMethod pointed at admin REST (/wp-json/wp/v2/product) with expectedProductCount=11370 — matches DB pattern and aligns with bootstrap dataFlow which discovers via admin REST.

DB's 2-step dataFlow (discover via admin REST 11370, enrich price/stock via Store API) is the correct pattern for this site precisely because the Store API hides OOS items by default. R1's single-endpoint shape would miss 6877 out-of-stock published products from initial discovery. Recommend merging: keep DB's productDiscovery + priceEnrichment, retain R1's taxonomy + maxPerPage.
